limitations: Diagnostic only; final accumulators/output remain fp32, so this does not certify a double-output 1e-10 contract
Same-seed variant changes arithmetic representation while retaining the mathematical seed formulas; IEEE-double mantissa extraction replaces the two-float extraction
Frozen high/low coefficients are collapsed as double(hi)+double(lo); static inputs remain the same split geometry representation
Kernel-only warm medians use preallocated identical buffers, 256-thread blocks and 1048576 pairs; no search, assembly, transfer or complete solver step
GPU runs serialized, clocks/caches and desktop activity uncontrolled; library-math timings fluctuate and profile captures are reported separately
Broad replacement being slower does not exclude a speed benefit from a few selected fp64 operations
conclusion: Replacing the whole paired scalar core with native fp64 is about 2.9x slower canonical / 3.5x mixed in the same-seed test; lower register count does not compensate for fp64 compute throughput. Keep the paired core as a precision control and do not promote a wholesale fp64 replacement.
